question: How many flights were cancelled across the week in this data, and what was the most common reason?

content.text: I'll query the cancellation counts by code.

input.sql: SELECT count(*) AS total_flights, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status='cancelled') AS cancelled FROM flights
SELECT cancellation_code, count(*) AS n FROM flights WHERE status='cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT flight_date, count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE cancellation_code='C') nas, count(*) FILTER (WHERE cancellation_code='B') wx, count(*) FILTER (WHERE cancellation_code='A') carrier FROM flights WHERE status='cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT origin, count(*) n, string_agg(DISTINCT cancellation_code,',') codes FROM flights WHERE status='cancelled' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 8

content.text:
106 WN flights cancelled out of 26,161 scheduled in the 1–7 Jan window, or 0.41%.

The dominant reason is national airspace system (code C), 65 cancellations — 61% of the total. Weather (code B) is second with 27, and carrier (code A) third with 14. No security cancellations.

Two dates carry almost the whole week:

- **3 Jan — 55 cancellations, 52 of them NAS.** This is the single worst day and effectively defines the "most common reason" answer; strip this day out and NAS falls to 13 for the rest of the week.
- **1 Jan — 29 cancellations, 25 of them weather.** Nearly all of the week's weather cancellations land on New Year's Day.

The remaining five days total 22 cancellations combined, and 6–7 Jan are clean (3 and 1, all carrier-coded).

By station, the concentration is SAN with 19 (mix of B and C), SJU with 18 (all C), and PSP with 9. SJU being entirely NAS-coded on a single-cause basis is consistent with a routing or airspace constraint rather than local weather, but the extract carries no weather or ATC-advisory data, so I can't confirm the underlying driver — only how the carrier coded it.
